nodes.label: Trade-In Decision Boundary
nodes.rationale: UltimatePOS stays the authority for the financial acquisition, stock quantity, balances, payments and accounting callbacks; Recommerce owns physical device identity, identifier history, ownership/custody periods, lifecycle state and the link explaining which financial source acquired the device. Trade-in must not create a Recommerce-only purchase, payment, balance or stock ledger, and an offer is an estimate until an authorised acceptance posts an authoritative POS transaction.

nodes.label: TradeInPricingService
nodes.rationale: A versioned, deterministic rule engine recording all inputs, reserves, calculation version, recommendation levels, inspection and manual market evidence in an immutable valuation snapshot. It deliberately does not encode a historic fixed 30/20/10 formula, and ML, opaque AI prices, scraping and live feeds are deferred so V1 stays explainable.

nodes.label: TradeInService accept()
nodes.rationale: Invokes UltimatePosPurchaseWriter once with one unit at the accepted price and creates no payment, so native settlement can remain due. Only after the native receipt returns in the same transaction does it append the acquisition row, close customer periods, open business/location periods, record movement and lifecycle evidence and set the Device AVAILABLE / ON_HAND.

nodes.label: recommerce_device_acquisitions Append-Only Table
nodes.rationale: A separate append-only acquisition record is required because recommerce_device_purchase_assignments has a unique device_id and describes the first received purchase layer; reusing it would destroy the original acquisition history needed for repeat sale to trade-in to resale cycles.

nodes.label: UltimatePosPurchaseWriter (Trade-In Reuse)
nodes.rationale: Creates a native received purchase transaction and purchase_lines row, adjusts stock through ProductUtil, recalculates payment status, writes activity and dispatches PurchaseCreatedOrModified, deliberately creating no payment row so settlement stays a separate native operation.

nodes.label: Native Settlement Proof
nodes.rationale: Settling the accepted trade-in's purchase through the native TransactionPaymentController path moved payment_status due to paid while every trade-in-scoped Recommerce row stayed byte-identical, proving the deferred-settlement boundary. The record also documents a shell word-splitting error that produced a false 'unchanged' diff and seeder noise that forced per-table scoping.

nodes.label: Trade-In Reversal and Reconciliation Contract
nodes.rationale: A posted native purchase is reversed only through the ordinary UltimatePOS purchase-return/void authority; Recommerce then appends an inverse movement and never deletes original rows. Reversal is refused after a subsequent sale, transfer or repair custody change, and reconciliation must report missing, duplicate, due/paid or reversed links as blocking evidence without auto-balancing stock or inventing a cost.

nodes.label: Known Limitation: Reversal Has No User Interface
nodes.rationale: TradeInService::recordReversal is implemented, permission-gated and test-covered, but has no route, controller action or view, so an operator cannot reverse an accepted trade-in and a browser reversal proof is impossible rather than merely outstanding. Building it needs a decision on how the native purchase-return reference is supplied and confirmed.

nodes.label: Mutation-Checked Required-Test Closure
nodes.rationale: Five added tests each name the deliberate service mutation that turns them red, exposing a first reuse test that passed equally when prior periods were deleted. Closure is scoped honestly: concurrency is asserted through the status gate rather than two live connections because in-memory SQLite offers no second connection, and duplicate strong identifiers are prevented structurally because TradeInService never creates a Device or DeviceIdentifier.

nodes.label: Deny-By-Default Trade-In Permissions
nodes.rationale: view, manage, approve, override_economic_ceiling, accept and reverse are new permissions whose registration does not silently grant them to existing roles.
